unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U03: Apply co-surety contribution without enlarging the loss

payload.stem_md: For a stipulated equal-contribution exercise, the creditor has recovered part of the guaranteed loss from the principal debtor. One co-surety proposes dividing the original gross loss without crediting that recovery. What is required?

options.text_md: Ignore every recovery from the principal debtor
options.explanation_md: That risks overstating the net amount.

options.text_md: Reconcile the net unrecovered amount before the stipulated contribution allocation
options.explanation_md: The exercise must credit the stated recovery once.

options.text_md: Treat every co-surety as liable beyond all agreed limits

payload.correct_explanation_md: The exercise must credit the stated recovery once.

payload.stem_md: The exercise stipulates equal contribution subject to each undertaking limit. A draft says equal sharing automatically overrides a smaller legal limit. Which principle is relevant?

options.text_md: The applicable undertaking limits still require analysis
options.explanation_md: Equality is not permission to enlarge a surety undertaking.

options.text_md: Every limit becomes void when another surety pays
No co-surety can ever seek contribution
options.explanation_md: The source recognises the qualified right.

options.text_md: Only the bank loan number determines the share
options.explanation_md: It does not establish the allocation.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Equality is not permission to enlarge a surety undertaking.

payload.title: Contribution after partial recovery
payload.scenario_narrative_md: A surety has paid the creditor and now seeks co-surety contribution. The exercise stipulates equal sharing in the absence of a contrary contract, but preserves undertaking limits. A principal-debtor recovery must be credited before any net allocation. Identify the two controls needed to avoid an overstated claim.
